winning_patterns: Short 12-22 second clips with immediate payoff hooks like 'lasted three seconds' or 'helicopter exploded' outperformed 23-35 second clips by nearly 2x median views.
Top clips featured high-energy streamers without facecams reacting to chaotic GTA 6 physics failures, explosions, or instant deaths rather than slow gameplay.
YouTube Shorts drove 90% of total views, so clips must be optimized for YouTube's Shorts feed first with fast cuts and no slow intros.
avoid_patterns: Reject any clip longer than 30 seconds with zero views, such as GTA-027 'XQC GTA 6 MASSAGGATOR BC CRASH' at 30.04 seconds.
Reject vague, incomplete hooks like 'this is a' (GTA-024) that fail to establish conflict or payoff within the first 2 seconds.
Reject all-caps clickbait titles like 'JYNXZI CAN'T STEAL FERRARI' (GTA-030) that overpromise and underdeliver on actual chaos.
hook_style_guidance: Write Frame-1 hooks that name the streamer and the specific chaotic event in under 8 words, using present-tense action verbs and zero setup.
daily_brief: The ohnepixel bridge clip earned 10,272 views by delivering instant chaos in 13.71 seconds, proving short, high-energy clips win on YouTube Shorts. The 30-second flops with 0-1 views show that slow pacing and vague hooks kill retention. Tomorrow, cut all clips to 12-18 seconds with immediate payoff hooks and prioritize YouTube Shorts distribution.
